aining defect is that a bought pad is only hidden, not cleaned up. Its SurfaceGui/BillboardGui keeps the label and price text (pad.label and pad.cost are never cleared), and the price colouring in refresh runs on non-visible pads too. Any check or extra overlay that reads the pad's label text, such as the PadFeedbackService overlay, still sees the buy label and price. Pads that are hidden only by the MAX_VISIBLE window or a requires gate behave the same way.
Evidence: Source read via probes: purchase() sets state.owned[id]=true and hides the pad by Transparency, CanTouch and gui.Enabled only. The shop handler and the pad Touched handler both route through purchase(). refresh() recolours pad.cost for every pad, including hidden ones, and never clears or destroys the label and price. I did not run a probe confirming which element is still visible.
Fix hint: In purchase() and in refresh() for non-visible or owned pads, fully remove the pad's presentation: destroy pad.gui (or set label.Text and cost.Text to empty and Visible=false) and skip the cost recolouring. Also make sure PadFeedbackService.Unregister removes any overlay it added. Make refresh the single source of truth for pad visibility from state.owned.

## Lessons from past builds
# Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull. Keep the second purchase within about 20-30s of idle income, by raising per-item value or lowering the price. Chain the first few upgrades so there is always something affordable to chase in the first minute, with no long dead gaps.
- Starting cash must be strictly below the first upgrade's price, never equal to it. An instant spend gives the player no chase and no sense of what cubes are for. Start slightly below the price so the first few collected cubes earn it, within about 10s. Check starter cash against the first cost in config before finishing.
- The first purchase must actually happen in a short playtest, and its counters (e.g. upgrades_bought) must be above 0. If the report lacks them, the first pad is too hard to find or reach. A highlight or "affordable" counter above 0 with no purchase counter means the pad was reachable in logic but the player never touched it. Put the first pad close to where the player stands after claiming (just off the walking path), and guide the player to it with a beam. Make sure the tutorial step that points to it fires.
- Assume the playtest player may stand idle. Enough cash alone is not enough: the first pad must be within a few studs of the post-claim position, or a fallback must buy or prompt the first upgrade after the player has been able to afford it for a few seconds. Otherwise the purchase loop goes untested even though cubes were collected.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases. Add a visible next-goal indicator, such as a progress bar toward the next affordable upgrade, and pulse the cash counter on each gain.
- Give failure feedback as well as success feedback. A pad, button, shop purchase or rebirth attempted without enough cash, or a shop card whose requirement is not owned, needs a red flash, an audible buzz, a shake and a "Need $N" or requirement toast, debounced to about 1s. Never return silently from a denied Buy handler. A silent denial confuses young players.
- Place trigger pads (buy pads, claim gates, etc.) off the spawn path so walking from spawn never fires them accidentally. They must

## UI kit (house style for all UI: paste the snippets you use, Theme first, and adapt; plain Luau, not modules)
- Chunky text: every label gets a dark UIStroke (2.5-4 px). LuckiestGuy for titles/numbers, FredokaOne for body. Never default or thin fonts.
- One palette everywhere: yellow Primary = main action, green Good = affordable/claim, red Bad = close/can't, blue Info = secondary, dark Ink outlines.
- Depth: UICorner 12-18 px, UIStroke border, light-top UIGradient fill, hard drop shadow 4-6 px below.
- Everything moves: appear with a Back-eased UIScale pop (0 -> 1), react with a punch (1.2 -> 1), press squish to 0.9. Tween UIScale, not Size; 0.1-0.4 s, never linear.
- Numbers tick up and pop on change, big values short ("12.5K"); gains flash green, losses red.
- Every action gives feedback: toast, floating "+N" or reward popup. Max 3 toasts.
- Mobile first: 1280x720 offsets under a viewport UIScale (`Theme.screen`), safe insets, buttons >= 44 px, nothing key in the top-left (Roblox menu).
- HUD hugs the edges, centre stays clear; windows open over a dim backdrop with a close X.
- World prices on BillboardGuis: green when affordable, red when not.
- UI is built in code with Instance.new, no image asset ids (emoji/letters for icons), ResetOnSpawn = false.

### PriceBillboard.luau (World price tag on a buy pad / shop item (BillboardGui), green when affordable. Works in server Scripts.)
```luau
-- PriceBillboard: world price tag over a buy pad / shop item; green when affordable, red when not. Server or client.
-- Standalone (no Theme needed) so a server Script can paste it too.
local function priceBillboard(part: BasePart, title: string, price: number): (BillboardGui, (boolean) -> ())
	local bb = Instance.new("BillboardGui")
	bb.Size, bb.StudsOffset = UDim2.fromScale(6, 2.2), Vector3.new(0, part.Size.Y / 2 + 2, 0)
	bb.AlwaysOnTop, bb.MaxDistance, bb.LightInfluence = false, 80, 0
	bb.Adornee = part
	local function text(t: string, y: number, h: number, color: Color3): TextLabel
		local l = Instance.new("TextLabel")
		l.Size, l.Position, l.BackgroundTransparency = UDim2.fromScale(1, h), UDim2.fromScale(0, y), 1
		l.Text, l.Font, l.TextScaled, l.TextColor3 = t, Enum.Font.LuckiestGuy, true, color
		local s = Instance.new("UIStroke")
		s.Thickness, s.Color = 3, Color3.fromRGB(28, 22, 38)
		s.Parent = l
		l.Parent = bb
		return l
	end
	text(title, 0, 0.45, Color3.fromRGB(255, 248, 232))
	local cost = text("$" .. tostring(price), 0.45, 0.55, Color3.fromRGB(240, 68, 64))
	bb.Parent = part
	local function setAffordable(ok: boolean)
		cost.TextColor3 = if ok then Color3.fromRGB(88, 214, 92) else Color3.fromRGB(240, 68, 64)
	end
	return bb, setAffordable -- client: call setAffordable(cash.Value >= price) on cash.Changed
end
```
